events.title: Will Dardo be named Fnatic LoL General Manager by...?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Javier "Dardo" Zafra is officially announced as the next permanent General Manager of Fnatic's League of Legends team by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Appointments of "interim," "acting," or other non-permanent General Managers will not count. Appointments to any other role at Fnatic (e.g., Team Director, or a role outside Fnatic's League of Legends team) will not count unless the official announcement names him General Manager of Fnatic's League of Legends team.

An official announcement of the appointment made by the listed date will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of when the appointment goes into effect.

If another person is officially announced as the next permanent General Manager of Fnatic's League of Legends team before Dardo is, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Fnatic; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

events.title: Worlds 2026 Winning Region
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the region or country of the esports team winning 1st place in the League of Legends 2026 Season World Championship (Worlds 2026).

If the winner of Worlds 2026 is not determined by December 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Fandom (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship).

Regions counted in World 2026:
- LCK (South Korea)
- LPL (China)
- LEC (Europe / EMEA)
- LCP (Asia-Pacific)
- LCS (North America)
- CBLOL (Brazil)

events.title: LoL Offseason: Diable Next Team
events.description:
This market will resolve to the next team Diable officially joins by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

If Diable does not officially join a new team by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Diable joins a team that is not listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Diable retires or is not under contract with any professional team by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

Diable's current team, Nongshim RedForce, is not listed. A contract extension or re-signing with Nongshim RedForce does not count as joining a new team.

Only a signing as a player to a team's main League of Legends roster will count. Signings to academy or development rosters, or to non-player roles (e.g., coach, analyst, or content creator), will not count.

For the purposes of this market, Diable is considered to have officially joined a team once his signing is officially announced by the team or by Diable; the announcement must be made by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. The date his contract takes effect, his registration on an official league roster, and the date of his first match for the team will not be considered. Market titles refer to the team Diable joins for the 2027 season, and resolve per these rules.

An official signing announcement prior to the market's close date will immediately resolve this market to the corresponding option.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official announcements from the acquiring team. A consensus of credible media reporting may also be used to resolve the market.

events.title: Worlds 2026: Winner
events.description:

If multiple teams are declared winners, this market will resolve in favor of the team whose listed team name comes first alphabetically.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.

events.title: Region with the Most Teams in the Worlds 2026 Knockout Stage
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the region with the most teams in the Knockout Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026.

A team counts for the region (league) through which it qualified for Worlds 2026: LCK (South Korea), LPL (China), LEC (Europe / EMEA), LCS (North America), LCP (Asia-Pacific), or CBLOL (Brazil). A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through. A team is considered to have reached the Knockout Stage if it is officially confirmed as one of the eight teams advancing from the Swiss Stage to the Knockout Stage (quarterfinals).

If two or more regions are tied for the most teams in the Knockout Stage, this market will resolve to "Tie".

If the eight Knockout Stage teams have not been determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed team finishes the Swiss Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026) with a 0-3 match record, meaning it loses each of its first three Swiss Stage matches and is eliminated. Worlds 2026 is currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026, with the Swiss Stage scheduled for October 23 to October 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Match records count series results, not individual games: each Swiss Stage match counts once, whether it is played as a Bo1 or a Bo3. Forfeits and other administrative results count as officially recorded by Riot Games.

If the listed team wins any Swiss Stage match, does not compete in the Swiss Stage (e.g. it is eliminated in the Play-In), or it otherwise becomes impossible for the listed team to finish the Swiss Stage 0-3, the associated market will resolve to "No".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, postponed after December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the Swiss Stage results have not been determined within this timeframe, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.

events.title: Will a European team reach the Worlds 2026 Knockout Stage?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one European team reaches the Knockout Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A European team is a team that qualified for the tournament through the LEC (Europe / EMEA). Teams that qualified through the LCK, the LPL, the LCS, the LCP, or the CBLOL are not European teams. A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through. A team is considered to have reached the Knockout Stage if it is officially confirmed as one of the eight teams advancing from the Swiss Stage to the Knockout Stage (quarterfinals).

If the Knockout Stage field is not determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). events.title: Most Kills at Worlds 2026
events.description:
This market will resolve according to which player records the most total kills across all official games played during the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026.

Every completed official game of the tournament counts (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count unless their kills appear in the official tournament statistics. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

If two or more players are tied for the most kills, this market will resolve to the tied player with the fewer total deaths across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied player with the more total assists. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the player whose listed in-game name comes first alphabetically.

If a player not listed in this market records the most kills, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official tournament player statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, official information from Riot Games (https://lolesports.com) and a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Every completed official game of the tournament counts (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count unless their kills appear in the official tournament statistics. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

If two or more players are tied for the most kills, this market will resolve to the tied player with the fewer total deaths across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied player with the more total assists. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the player whose listed in-game name comes first alphabetically.

If a player not listed in this market records the most kills, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official tournament player statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, official information from Riot Games (https://lolesports.com) and a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Total Unique Champions Played at Worlds 2026
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the total number of unique champions played across all official games of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026, is greater than or equal to the number specified in the market title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A champion counts as "played" if it is picked and played by either team in at least one completed official game of the tournament (Play-In stage, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Champions that are only banned and never played do not count. Each champion counts once, regardless of how many times it is played.

Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count; however, a champion picked in such a game still counts if it is played in any other completed official game. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

If Worlds 2026 is canceled or postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the number of unique champions played in completed official games as of that time.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the tournament champion statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.question: Will a North American team reach the Worlds 2026 Knockout Stage?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one North American team reaches the Knockout Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A North American team is a team that qualified for the tournament through the LCS (North America). Teams that qualified through the LCK, the LPL, the LEC, the LCP, or the CBLOL are not North American teams. A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through. A team is considered to have reached the Knockout Stage if it is officially confirmed as one of the eight teams advancing from the Swiss Stage to the Knockout Stage (quarterfinals).

If the Knockout Stage field is not determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.

events.title: Which Teams Will Make a Roster Change Before December?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any player joins or leaves the listed team's active League of Legends roster (defined as the active lineup listed on the listed team's Liquipedia page) by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The relevant roster is whichever active lineup is listed on the resolution source at market creation. Name changes or aliases referring to the same player do not qualify as roster changes.

For the purpose of this market, "roster change" refers to any official signing, transfer, benching to inactive/reserve, release, retirement, or departure of a player from the active lineup. This includes adding new players (transfers, free agent signings, or loans), removing players (to inactive, free agency, or other teams), or any change resulting in a different active roster.

A qualifying roster change must occur on or before the deadline, and be reflected in the resolution source. Once the change appears in the resolution source, it must remain live for at least 48 continuous hours to be valid. This 48-hour period may finish after the deadline, so long as the change itself occurred on or before the deadline. If the change is reverted or removed before 48 hours have elapsed, the window resets and will not count toward resolution.

Coach changes and temporary stand-ins for a single match will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be Liquipedia; however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any player joins or leaves the listed team's active League of Legends roster (defined as the active lineup listed on the listed team's Liquipedia page) by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The relevant roster is whichever active lineup is listed on the resolution source at market creation. Name changes or aliases referring to the same player do not qualify as roster changes.

For the purpose of this market, "roster change" refers to any official signing, transfer, benching to inactive/reserve, release, retirement, or departure of a player from the active lineup. This includes adding new players (transfers, free agent signings, or loans), removing players (to inactive, free agency, or other teams), or any change resulting in a different active roster.

A qualifying roster change must occur on or before the deadline, and be reflected in the resolution source. Once the change appears in the resolution source, it must remain live for at least 48 continuous hours to be valid. This 48-hour period may finish after the deadline, so long as the change itself occurred on or before the deadline. If the change is reverted or removed before 48 hours have elapsed, the window resets and will not count toward resolution.

Coach changes and temporary stand-ins for a single match will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be Liquipedia; however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: How many Pentakills will there be at Worlds 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the total number of pentakills recorded across all official games of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026, is greater than or equal to the number specified in the market title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A pentakill is a single player killing all five players on the opposing team in quick succession, as announced by the game client ("PENTAKILL") and recorded in the official game statistics. Every completed official game of the tournament counts (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Pentakills in games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count.

If Worlds 2026 is canceled or postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the number of pentakills recorded in completed official games as of that time.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the tournament statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, official information from Riot Games (https://lolesports.com) and a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: League of Legends Global Power Rankings Post Worlds: Rank 1
events.description:
This market will resolve to the team ranked number 1 on the Global Power Rankings at the end of the 2026 competitive year.

The market resolves to whichever team occupies the number 1 position on the official Global Power Rankings once the final 2026 ranking is published following the conclusion of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship.

If two or more teams are tied for number 1 on the final 2026 ranking, this market will resolve in favor of the team whose listed team name comes first alphabetically. If a team not individually listed as an outcome finishes number 1, this market will resolve to "Other."

If the final 2026 Global Power Rankings are not published, or a number 1 team is not determined, by January 14, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other."

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the League of Legends Esports Global Power Rankings (https://lolesports.com/en-GB/gpr/2026/current); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Most Played Champion at Worlds 2026
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the champion that is played in the most official games during the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026.

A champion is "played" in a game when it is picked and played by either team in a completed official game of the tournament (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Bans do not count as plays. Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

In the case of a tie, this market will resolve to the tied champion with the higher win rate across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied champion with more bans across the tournament. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the champion whose name comes first alphabetically.

If a champion not listed in this market is the most played, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the tournament champion statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Will Caedrel Reach Challenger Before the End of the Year?
events.description:
This market will resolve "Yes" if Caedrel reaches the Challenger rank in League of Legends solo/duo ranked queue on any server on or before December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

"Reaching Challenger" means Caedrel's account attains the Challenger tier in the ranked solo/duo queue, as displayed in the official in-game ranked ladder or on his verified account, at any point during the market period. Reaching Challenger in flex queue does not count unless otherwise specified.

The account must be one publicly identified as belonging to Caedrel and streamed or otherwise confirmed as his. Reaching Challenger on a smurf or alternate account still counts, provided it is verifiably his and he publicly demonstrates it (e.g., on stream). If Caedrel is confirmed to have reached Challenger at any point in the period — even briefly — this market resolves "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be the official League of Legends ranked ladder (via the in-game client or op.gg / official Riot data for his verified account) and Caedrel's official streams or channels; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Will Chovy leave Gen.G in 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Chovy departs Gen.G's active League of Legends roster by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, Chovy is considered to have "left" if he is officially removed from Gen.G's active roster — including a transfer to another team, release, contract termination, benching to inactive/reserve status, loan to another team, retirement, or any other departure from the active lineup — as reflected on Gen.G's Liquipedia page (https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/Gen.G). An official announcement by Gen.G by the deadline that Chovy has departed the team, or will not be part of Gen.G's roster for the 2027 season, will also count as leaving.

The change must occur by the deadline and be reflected in the resolution source. Once the departure appears in the resolution source, it must remain in effect for at least 48 continuous hours to be valid. This 48-hour period may finish after the deadline, so long as the departure itself occurred by the deadline. If the change is reverted before 48 hours have elapsed, it will not count toward resolution.

A name change or alias referring to the same player on the same team does not count as leaving. Temporary absence for a single match (with the player remaining on the roster) does not count.

If Gen.G disbands, or Chovy and Gen.G part ways because the roster is dissolved, this will count as the player leaving and resolve "Yes".

The primary resolution source for this market will be Liquipedia; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Will more than one Western team reach the Worlds 2026 Knockout Stage?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if two or more Western teams reach the Knockout Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Teams that qualified through the LCK (South Korea), the LPL (China), or the LCP (Asia-Pacific) are not Western teams. A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through. events.title: Worlds 2026: Grand Final Region Matchup
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the regional matchup of the Grand Final of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for November 14, 2026, in New York City.

If the Grand Final participants are not determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). A team's region is the league through which it qualified for Worlds 2026: the LCK (South Korea), the LPL (China), the LEC (Europe / EMEA), the LCS (North America), the LCP (Asia-Pacific), or the CBLOL (Brazil). A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through.

"LCK vs LCK" corresponds to a Grand Final between two LCK teams, "LCK vs LPL" to a Grand Final between one LCK team and one LPL team, and "LPL vs LPL" to a Grand Final between two LPL teams. If the Grand Final is any other matchup, including any matchup involving a team from the LEC, LCS, LCP, or CBLOL, this market will resolve to "Other".

Only the two teams officially confirmed as the participants in the Grand Final match matter; the outcome of the Grand Final does not matter.

If the Grand Final participants are not determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.

events.title: Worlds 2026: Grand Final Series Score
events.description:
Each market in this group will resolve to "Yes" if the Grand Final of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for November 14, 2026, in New York City, ends with the listed series score, regardless of which team wins. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No". The Grand Final is a best-of-five series.

"3-0" means the winning team wins three games without losing a game, "3-1" means the winning team wins three games and loses one game, and "3-2" means the winning team wins three games and loses two games.

Only completed, officially recorded games count. A game that is remade or restarted before completion counts once, as the completed game. If any game of the Grand Final is awarded by forfeit or administrative decision without being played to completion, every market in this group will resolve to "No".

If the Grand Final has not been completed by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, every market in this group will resolve to "No".

events.title: Will G2 Caps Get a Hair Transplant in 2026?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Rasmus "Caps" Borregaard Winther undergoes a hair transplant procedure before December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A hair transplant procedure means a surgical hair restoration procedure in which hair follicles are moved or implanted to the scalp, including follicular unit extraction (FUE), follicular unit transplantation (FUT), and any other surgical grafting technique. Non-surgical treatments, including medication, topical treatments, platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections, laser therapy, scalp micropigmentation, hair systems, wigs, and hairpieces, will not qualify. Shaving, regrowing, or otherwise changing the length or style of his hair will not qualify.

The procedure must actually take place within the window above. An announcement that Caps intends or plans to undergo a hair transplant will not qualify on its own, and a procedure that took place before market creation will not qualify regardless of when it is disclosed. Whether the procedure is successful, and whether any transplanted hair later grows or is visible, is irrelevant.

A qualifying procedure must be established by a public statement from Caps or his official representatives, an official statement from his team, or a consensus of credible reporting. Statements made in jest, satire, or parody content, and speculation based only on changes in Caps' appearance, will not qualify.

Information published on or before January 1, 2027, 11:59 PM ET may be used to establish that a qualifying procedure took place within the window above; a qualifying procedure first established after that time will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Caps and G2 Esports; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: LoL: G2 Esports vs Dplus KIA (BO1) - Worlds Group Stage
events.description:
This market refers to the LoL Round 1 match between G2 Esports and Dplus KIA in the Worlds Group Stage, initially scheduled for October 23, 2026 at 4:00 PM ET.

This market will resolve to "G2 Esports" if G2 Esports win the match against Dplus KIA.

This market will resolve to "Dplus KIA" if Dplus KIA win the match against G2 Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or ends in a tie, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before November 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of October 23, 2026 at 4:00 PM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

markets.question: Game 5: Odd/Even Total Kills?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Odd" if the total combined kills by both teams in Game 5 is an odd number.

This market will resolve to "Even" if the total combined kills by both teams in Game 5 is an even number.

"Total combined kills" includes all champion kills recorded during the match by both Contingent Esports and University of Mississippi. Executions (deaths to non-champion sources such as turrets, minions, or neutral monsters where no enemy champion receives kill credit) do not count as kills for the purposes of this market.

If no kills are recorded in Game 5, or if Game 5 is canceled (not played at all), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before September 10, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of August 27, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

If Game 5 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 5 is not played because the series result has already been determined (e.g., a team clinches the series before Game 5 is needed), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 5 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead.
